You answer a question about machinery and work-equipment law using ONLY the numbered facts given.
Each fact has a subject, a relation, a value (as written, then in normal form in brackets), sometimes a condition,
and the place it comes from. Some facts carry a note computed from the dates: trust the notes.

Rules:
- Use only these facts. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere.
- If the facts do not answer the question, the kind is "unknown" and the value is null.
- A condition attached to a fact is part of the fact: carry it into the answer.
- If the question asks about a day, compare that day with every date in the facts, one by one, before you answer.
  A repeal, a limit or an application "from" a date takes effect on that date, not earlier: an act repealed from a
  date is still fully in force, with everything it permits, on every earlier day; a rule applying from a date does
  not yet bind on earlier days.
- If a note says that a date quoted in a condition was corrected, reason with the corrected date.
- If the question asks "which" or "what" and several facts answer it, list every one of them, in the words of the
  facts, one item per fact. Facts filed under the same article, annex part or numbered point belong together.
  When the answer is a group named by an article or an annex part and the facts list the members of that group,
  give the members, not the name of the group.
- A fact noted as "filed under a place the question names" belongs to the answer of a "which / what" question
  about that place whenever its relation fits the question: list all of them, not one.
- Lines under "Computed by rule" are results worked out in code from the numbered facts they name: trust them,
  give their result as the answer for the device asked about, and put the fact numbers they name in "used".
- Include only what the question asks for: no neighbouring item, no other regime that the question did not ask
  about. An option that combines several things in sequence is one item, not several.
- A fact about a neighbouring subject (another paragraph, another device, another kind of verification, another
  product, another deadline) does not answer the question. When the exact subject asked about is absent from the
  facts, "unknown" is the correct answer: do not answer from the nearest fact.
- For a "who" question, when one fact, or several facts with the same subject and relation, name several bodies,
  all of them are the answer together: name each one.
- For "which categories / which items listed in a place", the answer is the members filed under that place, each
  in the words of its fact, without adding the place to the item.
- For "which risks / which hazards does a numbered point address", use every fact filed under that point whatever
  its relation: a measure is required against a risk, and its subject and condition name that risk.
- Never return a list for a "text" answer: a question that one sentence answers (who, why, how, under which
  condition, which one thing and why) gets one short sentence. "Which / what / list all" of several things is "set".
- Facts marked "matched by relation" were found by querying the facts by their relation, subject and place:
  prefer them. When the question asks for all of something, the answer is the list of their subjects or values,
  one item per fact, nothing merged and nothing dropped. If the matched facts answer the question, do not add
  items from the other facts, which are context.
- The kind follows the question: "from which date / when (a day)" is "date"; "for how long" alone is "duration";
  "can / may / is / does" is "boolean"; "which / what (several things)" is "set"; who, why, under which condition,
  or who does something and within what time is "text", and the text names every element asked for.
- Return JSON only, with the reasoning first:
  {"reasoning": "the facts and dates compared, step by step, in a few short sentences",
   "kind": "set|date|duration|boolean|text|unknown",
   "value": <list of short strings for set | "YYYY-MM-DD" for date | ISO 8601 duration like "P10Y" | true/false | a short text | null>,
   "text": "one or two sentences for a person, naming the article or annex point",
   "used": [fact numbers you relied on]}

Question: Who is considered the manufacturer after a substantial modification of machinery?

[2] manufacturer — becomesManufacturer — markets those products under its name or trademark (markets those products under its name or trademark) [condition: manufactures products within the scope of this Regulation or who has those products designed or manufactured] [REG, Art. 3(18)] [matched by relation]
[3] natural or legal person carrying out substantial modification — hasObligation — shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in Article 10 (shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in article 10) [condition: if the substantial modification has an impact on the safety of only machinery or a related product that is part of an assembly of machinery] [REG, Art. 18]
[4] substantial modification — definedAs — a modification of machinery or a related product, by physical or digital means after that machinery or related product has been placed on the market or put into service, which is not foreseen or planned by the manufacturer, and which affects the safety of that machinery or related product, by creating a new hazard, or by increasing an existing risk, which requires: (a) the addition of guards or protective devices to that machinery or related product the processing of which necessitates the modification of the existing safety control system; or (b) the adoption of additional protective measures to ensure the stability or mechanical strength of that machinery or related product (a modification of machinery or a related product, by physical or digital means after that machinery or related product has been placed on the market or put into service, which is not foreseen or planned by the manufacturer, and which affects the safety of that machinery or related product, by creating a new hazard, or by increasing an existing risk, which requires: (a) the addition of guards or protective devices to that machinery or related product the processing of which necessitates the modification of the existing safety control system; or (b) the adoption of additional protective measures to ensure the stability or mechanical strength of that machinery or related product) [condition: which is not foreseen or planned by the manufacturer] [REG, Art. 3(16)]
[5] any natural or legal person who places on the market or puts into service machinery — becomesManufacturer — shall be considered a manufacturer (shall be considered a manufacturer) [condition: In the absence of a manufacturer as defined above] [DIR, Art. 2]
[6] manufacturer — definedAs — any natural or legal person who designs and/or manufactures machinery or partly completed machinery covered by this Directive and is responsible for the conformity of the machinery or the partly completed machinery with this Directive with a view to its being placed on the market, under his own name or trademark or for his own use (any natural or legal person who designs and/or manufactures machinery or partly completed machinery covered by this Directive and is responsible for the conformity of the machinery or the partly completed machinery with this Directive with a view to its being placed on the market, under his own name or trademark or for his own use) [condition: under his own name or trademark or for his own use] [DIR, Art. 2]
[7] manufacturers of partly completed machinery — hasObligation — bears at least the designation of the partly completed machinery (bears at least the designation of the partly completed machinery) [REG, Art. 11(5)]
[8] the manufacturer — hasObligation — the appropriate measures shall be taken at the place of use by the manufacturer (the appropriate measures shall be taken at the place of use by the manufacturer) [condition: Where the machinery or related products cannot be assembled in the manufacturer’s premises] [REG, Annex III, 4.1.3]
[9] manufacturers of partly completed machinery — hasObligation — Manufacturers shall indicate their name (manufacturers shall indicate their name) [condition: where that is not possible, on its packaging or in a document accompanying the partly completed machinery] [REG, Art. 11(6)]
[10] manufacturers of partly completed machinery — hasObligation — shall immediately take the corrective actions necessary (shall immediately take the corrective actions necessary) [condition: Manufacturers who consider or have reason to believe that partly completed machinery which they have placed on the market is not in conformity with this Regulation] [REG, Art. 11(9)]
[11] manufacturer — hasObligation — the manufacturer shall: (a) determine the limits of the machinery or related product, which include the intended use and any reasonably foreseeable misuse thereof; (b) identify the hazards that may be generated by the machinery or related product and the associated hazardous situations; (c) estimate the risks, taking into account the severity of the possible injury or damage to health and the probability of its occurrence; (d) evaluate the risks, with a view to determining whether risk reduction is required, in accordance with the objective of this Regulation; (e) eliminate the hazards or reduce the risks associated with these hazards by application of protective measures, in the order of priority established in section 1.1.2(b) (the manufacturer shall: (a) determine the limits of the machinery or related product, which include the intended use and any reasonably foreseeable misuse thereof; (b) identify the hazards that may be generated by the machinery or related product and the associated hazardous situations; (c) estimate the risks, taking into account the severity of the possible injury or damage to health and the probability of its occurrence; (d) evaluate the risks, with a view to determining whether risk reduction is required, in accordance with the objective of this Regulation; (e) eliminate the hazards or reduce the risks associated with these hazards by application of protective measures, in the order of priority established in section 1.1.2(b)) [REG, Annex III]
